title: The launch-price card for a year's key
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **The "launch price ends November 30" card now also shows to anyone with PadSpan Pro or Bright Pro for a year**, once, until the end of November 30, with one more line: pay with the email your key was sent to and that key becomes Pro for life. A key that is already for life never sees it.

title: The usage report: its one question reaches every opt-in, and three things it could not say
body_markdown:
### New
- **The usage report says which store keeps PadSpan up to date, and whether your automations use it.** Two new lines in the opt-in report: `store`, one word for Home Assistant's Marketplace, HACS, or neither when PadSpan was copied in by hand; and `used_in`, how many automations and how many scripts use one of PadSpan's entities or devices. Two counts, never which ones. The Preview shows both, and the README's list of what the report sends has them.
- **Deleting PadSpan with the report on sends one last report that says so.** It carries the anonymous ID, the day, the version and that one flag, and nothing about the house, so a removed install can be told from a machine that is switched off. With the report off, nothing is sent.

### Changed
- **The optional question, where you heard about PadSpan, now reaches every way of opting in.** It was asked only after a yes on the opt-in card. It is now asked once per install whichever way the report comes on (the card, Settings, the tick box on the free trial) and when a free trial, a tester sign-up or a free year starts: a card on the Overview with one-tap answers and Skip. An answer or Skip ends it for good, it is never shown on a wall screen, and a house whose report was already on is still not asked: the choice stays under Settings → Tracking → Help improve PadSpan.

title: Room sets: odd-shaped rooms, doorways and kitchen corners; The launch price ends November 30; The usage report counts irk-capture keys apart; Live Aboard: Rooms ▾ by default; Usage report: Live Aboard's Look and rooms, and Furnish's room sets; WLED outputs: a made-up example address
body_markdown:
### New
- **One card on Overview: "The launch price ends November 30".** It says that PadSpan Pro for life is $89 CAD, once, until November 30 (then $168), with a button to buy at padspan.traks.ca. Only an administrator sees it, only on a house without a running paid licence (no key, a trial, or a licence that has run out), and only once: it is not shown again after a reload, and No thanks hides it for good. It is never shown on a wall screen, and it goes by itself at the end of November 30 (Pacific time). Nothing about it is sent in the usage report.

### Changed
- **The opt-in usage report now tells keys from an irk-capture ESP32 apart.** A key saved from an irk-capture ESP32 (in the phone wizard, or found by Auto-detect in the IRK Manager) is counted as one, with whether it works, and the report says how many irk-capture ESP32s Home Assistant has: counts only, never names, and only while the report is on.
- **Live Aboard shows one Rooms ▾ button at the top on every screen**, not a row of every room's name. It lists every named room under its floor's name, as before; pick one to go there. If you liked the row, tick **Room chips along the top** in ⋯ (on a wide screen; phones and wall screens always have Rooms ▾). Like the other ticks there, it is kept for that screen only.
- **The WLED card's network output hint shows a made-up example address (192.168.0.119).** It shows when a network output's address is missing or incomplete; before, its example was an address from a real network.

### Fixed
- **Room sets use the room's other walls before leaving a piece out.** In an L-shaped room a set could keep the bed and lose the wardrobe and the dresser. A piece with no room on the wall it was meant for now goes on another wall of the room. It still never overlaps anything, blocks a door or runs past a corner.
- **Room sets keep out of doorways.** A cabinet or a desk could stick partly into an opening with no door in it. Now nothing from a set stands in the way through a door or a doorway, on either side.
- **An L-shaped kitchen closes its corner.** When the walls didn't divide evenly, a gap was left where the two runs meet. Now the run is closed up to the corner with a unit sized to what is left (or the end unit made a little wider), and the worktop and wall cabinets run round the corner. The run along the side wall now starts right in the corner.
- **The bathroom set puts the basin under a window**, as the kitchen sets put the sink, when the toilet and basin already pass under one. Nothing is left out for it.
- **Hang on wall measures a sink or a basin to its worktop or rim.** It used to be measured to the top of its tap, so a sink hung under a low window went to another wall. Now it hangs under the window, with its tap in front of the glass, as when you drag it there.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- Counts of a Look picked in Live Aboard's Views ▾ (only its kind: Classic, Studio, a Showcase theme, or By the sun turned on), a room gone to from Rooms ▾ or from a room chip, and a room set placed in Furnish. Never which theme, room or set. Nothing is sent while the usage report is off.

title: The usage report can say where you heard about PadSpan; Doors and windows go with their room in Layout
body_markdown:
### New
- **One optional question after you opt in to the usage report: where did you hear about PadSpan?** When you turn the report on from the card, the same card asks it once, with one-tap answers (Reddit, YouTube, the Home Assistant forum, another forum, the Marketplace or HACS, GitHub, Discord, a web search, a friend, somewhere else) and a Skip button. It is not asked again. If your report is already on, nothing pops up: the same choice is under Settings → Tracking → Help improve PadSpan, where you can set, change or clear it. The answer goes with the report as one word (`heard_from`), it is your own answer and never worked out from anything, and the Preview shows it. The README's list of what the report sends has the new line.

### Changed
- **A room moved in Mapping → Layout takes its doors and windows with it.** Doors, windows and doorways drawn in Live Aboard used to stay where the old wall was when a room was moved, turned or reshaped in Layout, and stood there on their own. Now, when you press **Save corrections**, each one on that room's walls goes with it: same width, same heights and settings, same place along its wall (as far from the nearer corner as it was, never past a corner). One that can't follow stays where it is: its wall is gone or now too short, or it is in a wall the room shares with a room that didn't move the same way. The message after Save, and a line under the button, says how many moved and how many stayed, so you can check those in Live Aboard's **Edit**. Nothing new is stored in Live Aboard's file.

title: Live Aboard: going back by itself puts the bars aside; Licence and update checks: simpler
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **When nobody has touched it for a while, Live Aboard goes back home with the bars aside**, the map alone, as it opens. Before, it brought the bars back. Your walls, Look and floors pulled apart stay as you left them; ☰ brings the bars back. Home view in Views ▾ still brings them back, as it's pressed by hand.
- **Each licence check is one request again.** 0.38.259 sent a hash of Home Assistant's instance ID and, while the licence server didn't read it, asked a second time with the ID. Now the ID goes once, in the body of the request with the key (never in the web address). The licence server keeps only a hash of it, as before.
- **The update and licence checks run once a day.** 0.38.259 added a timer that looked every hour whether a day had passed. The first check after Home Assistant starts still waits a random while, and a restart doesn't check again within 20 hours.

title: Live Aboard: a look for each screen, room chips and a room panel; A sink under the window
body_markdown:
### New
- **A look for each screen.** Live Aboard's **Views ▾** has a new **Look** line: pick **Classic**, **Studio** or one of the Showcase themes, each shown with a small swatch of its colours. The screen you pick it on keeps it; **Same as Settings** puts it back to what Settings → Atlas → 🏠 Live Aboard says. Showcase themes come with PadSpan Bright Pro or PadSpan Pro, as on the flat Atlas.
- **One look by day, another after sunset.** In the same list, tick **By the sun** and pick a look for the day and one for after sunset. It switches by Home Assistant's sun.
- **Room chips.** Every named room is now along the top of Live Aboard, under its floor's name. Tap one and its floor shows, the view flies to the room and tints it, and its panel opens. On a phone and on a wall screen they are in **Rooms ▾**. They step aside with the bars when the map is alone.
- **A room panel beside the house.** A tap on a room's name opens its panel beside the house (at the bottom on a phone) instead of a sheet over the whole page, so you still see the room while you use it. It has the same lines and buttons as before, shows **Undo** after each switch, and lists **More devices of the area (n)**: what Home Assistant has in that room's area that the map doesn't show. Tap one for its own controls.

### Changed
- **The room you go to is tinted.** A room opened by a double-tap, a chip or its panel now has a light green tint on its floor, while the other rooms fade back as before.

### Fixed
- **A sink fits under a window.** A window's sill is measured against a sink's worktop (a basin's rim), not the top of its tap, which stands in front of the glass as a real one does. So a sink under a kitchen window gets no warning, and the kitchen room sets put the sink under a window when the base units pass under one. Room sets also keep wall cabinets off a window's glass.

title: Live Aboard opens on the whole house, labels by zoom level, Glass walls; Android phones: a warning when the transmitter is set too weak; Unlock asks first; white bulbs, Details and a live room sheet in the Atlas; Calibration tips that make the walk count; iPhone and Apple Watch keys from irk-capture, step by step; Licence and update checks, done more carefully; Drawing rooms: corners that line up, straight edges, overlaps named; Modern furniture; kitchens, bathrooms and one-tap room sets; People who are home stay in the house; A lighter Home Assistant database; Devices known only by their room, and room names, sit inside the room; Room changes in seconds, not a minute; A phone scan's doors and windows come into Live Aboard; The update dialog says what changed
body_markdown:
### New
- **Glass walls.** Walls has a fourth choice, **Glass**: the walls between you and the rooms turn into see-through tinted glass instead of being cut down, so each room keeps its height, and the walls at the back stay solid. Double-tap a room and the inside walls of its floor turn to glass too. The screen you pick it on keeps it, and it's also a line in ⋯ Show on this screen (**Glass walls**).
- **Labels by zoom level.** Looking at the whole house, each floor gets one tag beside it with its name and what's going on there ("Main · 3 lights on · 1 open · 2 people"); tap a tag to see that floor alone. On one floor you see room names, readings and sensor markers. Double-tap a room (or zoom in on it) and you see the device codes in that room while the other rooms fade back. Before, every name, reading, code and receiver showed at once. Leak, smoke, CO and gas alarms always show.
- **Track Your Phone warns when an Android phone sends too weakly.** Out of the box the Home Assistant Companion app sends at its lowest power, in its power-saving mode, and receivers barely hear it. When a phone's BLE Transmitter is set to Ultra low or Low transmit power, or to the Low power advertise mode, its row on the Overview now says so and what to set: Transmit power to High and Advertise mode to Low latency (Companion app → Settings → Companion app → Manage sensors → BLE Transmitter).
- **Warm or cool white for bulbs that do it.** Hold a light (or tap its code) on the Atlas: a bulb that can go from warm to cool white (Hue White Ambiance and the like) now has a colour temperature slider over its own range, plus Warm and Cool buttons when it has no colour. Before, it had brightness only. A colour bulb that also does white gets the slider beside its colour.
- **Details.** The bottom of a light's, fan's or lock's card has a Details link that opens Home Assistant's own window for it: history, settings and anything the card doesn't show. Not on a wall screen (`?kiosk=1`), where nothing leads off the page.
- **Who is in the room.** Tap a room's name: under its title the sheet now says who PadSpan places there ("Here: Alex, Sam"), the same people Overview's Occupancy card lists. Only on a screen that shows people: with Show people on (PadSpan Pro), and People left ticked in that screen's ⋯ list. Where people are hidden, the sheet names no one.
- **"I have an IRK Capture ESP32" is now five steps.** In Bluetooth → IRK Manager → Track your phone (with the Phone Setup Wizard or iPhone Setup Path on):
  1. Type the device's name and pick whose it is.
  2. Pick iPhone or Apple Watch and pair it: an iPhone in Settings → Bluetooth, a watch in its own Settings → Bluetooth under Health Devices.
  3. Press Find the key, then Save. If the key can't be found, paste it from the ESP32's IRK sensor.
  4. Remove the pairing again.
  5. Before the next device, press the ESP32's Refresh BLE Identity in Home Assistant, so the device you just paired doesn't connect to it again.
- **The key is saved under the name you typed**, and the device gets that name in PadSpan straight away, with its Home Assistant entities. With a person picked, it counts as that person's in the people count and in Live Aboard's People & devices.
- **Android phones are told this isn't their way in**: they don't keep sending this key in the background. They use the Companion app's BLE Transmitter.
- **Corners land on other rooms.** In Mapping → Edit, a room corner you click near another room's corner lands exactly on it; near another room's edge, it lands on the edge; otherwise, on a plan with a scale, it lands on a 5 cm grid. In Mapping → Layout a corner you drag does the same. Hold Alt to put a corner exactly where you click or drop it. On a scanned plan, a corner near a scanned wall end still lands on the wall end first.
- **Straighten edges.** A new button in Edit (Rooms tool) and in Layout. Every edge that is less than 5 cm off level or upright is made straight, and a corner another room shares moves with it, so a corner clicked 2 cm off no longer makes a slanted wall in 3D. Edges shorter than half a metre the other way are left alone, since a slant there may be meant. In Layout, "straight" means square to that floor's own walls, so a floor placed turned a degree or two is straightened to itself, not bent. It says how many edges it straightened, and nothing is saved until you press Save Layout (Edit) or Save corrections (Layout); Revert or Discard changes takes it back. In Edit it needs the plan's scale.
- **Rooms that overlap are named.** Edit and Layout now say, for example, "Kitchen and Pantry overlap, so the walls between them can't be drawn." It checks what is on screen, unsaved changes included. The usage report already counted these by number; now you see which rooms. In Edit this needs the plan's scale.
- **Help.** Mapping's Edit and Layout help now say how corners line up, how to place one freely with Alt, and what Straighten edges does (English, Deutsch, Français, Nederlands).
- **Kitchen furniture.** Build ▾ → Kitchen: base cabinets (doors, drawers, or a drawer over doors, each with its own worktop, so a row of them reads as one), wall cabinets (doors, glass, lift-up or open), tall cabinets (doors, a built-in oven, or an oven and a microwave), a sink with one or two bowls, a hob in the worktop or a freestanding cooker (induction or gas), a dishwasher and a fridge (tall, double or under the counter). A sink's height goes up to the top of its tap: a 1.2 m sink has its worktop at 0.9 m, level with the cabinets beside it.
- **Bathroom furniture.** Build ▾ → Bathroom: a toilet (on the floor, or hung on the wall), a basin (on a vanity unit, a pedestal or the wall; one or two), a bath (built-in or freestanding) and a shower (a glass enclosure, or a walk-in screen).
- **Room sets: furnish a room in one tap.** Build ▾ → Room sets puts a whole set in the room in the middle of the view: Kitchen, one wall; Kitchen, L-shaped; Bathroom; Bedroom; Living room; Dining room; Office. Pieces go along the walls with their backs against them, step past doors, windows and anything already there, and always stay inside the room. Anything that has no room is left out, and the message says how many. One Undo takes the whole set away. Nothing is kept until you Save.
- **15 new starter pieces** in the Library for the kitchen and the bathroom.
- **Import brings in a room scan's doors, windows and openings.** With RoomPlan import on (Settings → Features), Live Aboard's Furnish → Import used to take only the furniture and stairs from a RoomPlan scan, so every door and window had to be drawn again by hand. Now each door, window and opening in the scan (USDZ or JSON) comes in too, with its width, its height and, for a window, how high off the floor it starts. Heights are measured from the scanned room's floor.
  - A door comes in as a door (hinged left, swinging in, as a door you draw does), a window as a window.
  - An opening with no door in it that goes down to the floor (an archway) comes in as a doorway. One that starts higher up (a pass-through to the kitchen, say) comes in as a window at that height, listed as "Wall opening" so you can tell.
  - Each one goes on the nearest wall of the house, the same way doors and windows from a Sweet Home 3D file do. It keeps its width, moves along the wall only as far as it must to clear a corner or another door or window, and is cut only where the wall is too short for it.
  - It works best when the house's rooms were imported from the same scan, so the walls line up.

### Changed
- **Live Aboard opens on the whole house.** In the sidebar it now opens on every floor, pulled apart, with the page's bars out of the way so the house fills the window from the start. Tap ☰ (top right) to bring the bars back. If you had turned ⇕ Explode off, it stays off and the view opens on the floor with the most rooms, as before. A home view you set is still where it opens. Wall screens and Mapping open as they did.
- **A floor you pick stays picked.** Choosing a floor right after Live Aboard opens is no longer undone when the map finishes loading.
- **Unlock asks first.** Unlocking a door from the Atlas, the 3D house or a room's list now asks "Unlock Front Door?" with Unlock and Cancel. Cancel sends nothing. Lock never asks.
- **The room sheet keeps up.** While it is open it now shows the room as it is now, not as it was when you opened it. "All lights on" is there only while a light is off, and "All lights off" only while one is on; the fan buttons work the same way. They switch only the lights that would change.
- **Unavailable lights are greyed out.** A light Home Assistant can't reach says "Unavailable" in its card and in the room sheet, with its buttons and sliders greyed out, and "All lights on" leaves it alone.
- **Two tips wherever you calibrate.** Pin & Listen, Roam, Walk a room and Calibration's Results now say: carry the phone the way you usually do (in a pocket, screen off) and press the buttons on another phone, tablet or computer; and if you moved a receiver, calibrate the rooms next to it again. A phone in your hand with its screen on is heard differently from the same phone in your pocket, which is how PadSpan hears it the rest of the day.
- **Walk a room** no longer suggests holding the phone in your hand while you walk.
- **The licence check no longer puts your key or Home Assistant's instance ID in a web address.** Both now go in the body of the request. (This version sent a one-way hash of the ID and then asked again with the ID; from 0.38.261 it sends the ID once, as the licence server keeps only a hash of it.)
- **Starting the free trial sends the ID in the body of the request too, and claiming an invite sends no ID at all** (the licence server never used it there).
- **The daily checks wait a random while after Home Assistant starts** (5 minutes to 6 hours), and a restart within 20 hours of the last check doesn't check again. Homes that restart together after a Home Assistant release no longer all ask at the same moment.
- **PadSpan's requests say they come from PadSpan** (its own User-Agent instead of Home Assistant's default), and a server that answers "too many requests" is asked once more after the wait it names (at most a minute).
- **Furniture looks more modern.** Every piece has been redrawn in one cleaner style: lower and slimmer, with thin tapered legs, cabinets on a dark plinth set back so they seem to float, thinner tops with softened edges, and flush fronts with slim handles. Sofas have plump back cushions, the table lamp has a ceramic base, plants have real leaves, and the wood grain is finer. Your furniture keeps its own sizes, settings and colours; only the drawing is new. Cars and people are not changed.
- **New pieces start in calmer colours**: a grey sofa, light bedding, an oak table and chairs.
- **Signal readings are no longer stored in Home Assistant's history.** Every few seconds each tracked device's area sensor, distance sensors and tracker got a new signal strength, "seconds since heard" and confidence, and Home Assistant stored all of them each time. Those values are still shown on the entity, live, and automations can still use them; they are just not saved to the history database any more. The room, home or away, and the device's name are still saved, so history still shows where everything was. The occupancy sensor's per-room evidence and how sure it is are left out the same way.
- **A room change shows in seconds instead of over a minute.** Walk from the hall into the bedroom and PadSpan now shows the bedroom about 12 seconds later where the room's scanner hears well, and about 25 seconds later where it hears only now and then (a proxy left at ESPHome's standard scan settings catches about one advert in ten). With the house drawn on the map it takes a few seconds more. Before, a move took a minute and a half (median), and a short visit to a room was often never shown at all. Measured on simulated walks through PadSpan's own code, as no recorded walk with marked rooms exists yet. A device standing still switches rooms by mistake no more often than before, and far less often with the house drawn.
- **Every scanner is read on every update.** Home Assistant passes only the strongest scanner's adverts along as they arrive, so the others' readings were refreshed every 30 seconds and could be half a minute old. PadSpan now reads every scanner's list every 5 seconds, skipping adverts it already has, so it costs little more than before. Settings → Presence → Bluetooth refresh interval now defaults to 5 seconds.
- **Signal smoothing follows a real move at once.** When one scanner suddenly hears a device much more strongly, the device has moved, and PadSpan follows it straight away (and drops the readings of scanners that have heard nothing since). A reading that is suddenly much weaker on its own is usually a passing fade and only counts a little. The smoothing setting (Q) now defaults to 3, and the panel accepts up to 10; the old 0.125 was meant for smoothing each advert, many a second, not one update every 5 seconds.
- **A clear move next door needs half the Room Change Delay.** When the new room's scanner is well ahead of the old room's for two updates in a row, the device moves then. A close call, as by a doorway, still waits the whole Room Change Delay, and so do far-apart rooms, another floor and going outdoors.
- **Installs on the old defaults move to the new ones once.** If you never changed the smoothing (0.125) or the Bluetooth refresh interval (30 s), they become 3 and 5 s. A value you set yourself is kept.
- **The import says how many doors and windows have no wall to go on.** Any that are not near a wall of the house (more than 1 m away) are left out, and the line at the top of the list now counts them, for Sweet Home 3D files as well as scans. Each one is still listed with the reason.
- **The update dialog shows what changed.** Updating PadSpan HA from Home Assistant's Settings or from HACS used to show only "Release v0.38.x". It now shows the version's notes (for a stable release, every version since the last stable), how to update, and thanks to the people who reported what was fixed.

### Fixed
- **The Bluetooth screen no longer tells Android owners to look for a key.** It said the Companion app's BLE Transmitter holds an IRK; it doesn't, and an Android phone needs none, as the phone wizard already said. The IRK forms and their help now say the key is for iPhones and Apple Watches.
- **The phone guide** on padspan.traks.ca (English and German) no longer says to leave the transmitter's settings as they are.
- **A switch that failed in a room sheet no longer shows the new word.** A light's button there kept saying "On" when Home Assistant refused; it now goes back to what it was.
- **A white-only bulb no longer offers a colour picker** it can't use while it is on.
- **"Scan for IRK Capture devices" never read the ESP32.** It only looked at keys already paired with your Home Assistant computer, so a key from irk-capture had to be pasted by hand. PadSpan now reads the key the ESP32 shows in Home Assistant. It only reads: it never presses the ESP32's buttons or changes its settings.
- **Keys are no longer saved as "Auto-detected" or under the ESP32's name.** In the IRK Manager, Auto-detect IRKs puts a key from irk-capture in the Add an IRK box for you to name.
- **The IRK Capture tool card** on the ESPHome Configs tab no longer says it works for Android phones.
- **Home Assistants whose instance ID can't be read are no longer all one home.** Each sent the same stand-in to the licence server, so every such install counted as the same home on a key. Each now has its own random ID, made once and kept in PadSpan's settings (a Factory Reset keeps it).
- **People who are home no longer vanish from the 3D house or the people count.** PadSpan counted a Home Assistant person as home only when their state was exactly "home", so three kinds of people who were plainly in dropped out. Each now counts as home in Live Aboard and the flat Atlas, in the Occupancy count, in Vacation Mode's "pause while someone is home", and for Live Aboard's "Arrived home" card:
  - **Someone linked to PadSpan's own phone tracker**, as the phone guide says to do. That tracker reports the room, so the person reads "Kitchen", not "home".
  - **Someone with no tracker of their own** (their state is "unknown") whose phone or tag PadSpan hears in the house right now.
  - **Someone in a zone that lies inside your home zone**, such as a Garden zone in the yard, or whose state names the home zone itself.
- **Someone away still never counts as home:** "not_home", a zone anywhere else, or "unknown" with nothing of theirs heard. If a zone and a room share a name (an "Office" zone at work and an Office at home), the zone wins, so someone at work is never put in your office.
- **On the Overview's house map, devices known only by their room now sit inside that room, side by side.** They were all drawn on one point, the average of the room's corners. In an L-shaped room that point is outside the room, and every such device was stacked on it. Now the first sits at a point well inside the room and the next ones step out around it, apart from each other and from devices whose spot is known, the same way Live Aboard places people. Traceback's playback also puts a device known only by its room inside an L-shaped room.
- **An L-shaped room's name on the Overview's house map now sits inside the room.** It was drawn at the average of the room's corners, which for an L-shaped room is outside it. It now sits at the same point inside the room where that room's devices start.
- **A scanner that hears a device only now and then no longer moves it next door.** Twenty seconds without a new advert counted as the device having gone, even from a scanner that usually goes that long between adverts; the room's own scanner then faded and a still device was shown in the next room. Silence is now judged against that scanner's own gaps.
- **With the house drawn, a still device flickers between rooms far less.** Its worked-out position wanders a metre or so with the noise; it now has to be clearly inside the next room before it counts for it, as the strongest-scanner method already needed a 3 dB lead.
- **Each advert counts once.** A scanner's last reading was used again on every update while it was under 15 seconds old, so an old reading pulled harder than one reading should.
- **Replay & Score measures time in the recording's seconds.** The vote's "just arrived" rules read the clock while the replay ran, so in a replay every move looked like it came seconds after the last.

title: People and cars drawn again in Live Aboard
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Cars look like cars.** A car in the 3D house was a slab with a box on top. It now has a real side view with wheel arches cut into it, glass that leans in under a roof, and satin paint in place of shiny plastic. There are two characters:
  - **Sedan and Hatch: a low coupe.** A low nose with round lamps, one sweep of roof down to the tail, five-spoke wheels and a red light bar across the back.
  - **SUV and Pickup: a boxy 4x4.** A flat hood, round lamps at the ends of a dark grille with a bar of light between them, flared arches over big tyres, and a dark top. The SUV carries a spare on the back; the pickup has its bed.
- **People are tokens.** A person was a box with stick arms and legs. A person is now one smooth body in two colours (the top over the bottom) under a head: no arms or legs. Height, build, hair, glasses, cap and colours all still apply, and a child still has a bigger head for its height.
- Nothing needs setting up again. Each car keeps its size, colours, body style and charge-port light, and each person keeps their figure's settings.

title: Suggest a fit answers
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **"Suggest a fit" in Mapping → 3D Stack always said there was no fit** (0.38.256). It now works; expect it within about half a metre, to finish with the nudge buttons or Point Align.

title: Carry-along covers walls, beacons and sub-zones; Align can suggest a fit
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Carry-along offers only what stood on the plan when it was moved** and has not been touched since. Trimming, turning or extending a plan's picture is no move.

### Added
- **A moved plan's signal walls, fixed beacons and sub-zones can move with it.** Review in Mapping → Library now also lists the signal walls drawn in and along the plan's rooms, the fixed beacons standing in them and the sub-zones inside them, each unticked like the rest.
- **"Suggest a fit" in Mapping → 3D Stack.** Works out where a plan sits over the Reference plan's floor from the rooms drawn on both, and shows it for you to check: nothing is saved until you press Save. It needs two or more rooms on the plan and three or more on the other floor, and stays silent rather than guess. One room alone is never fitted this way: use Point Align.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- Which of walls, beacons and sub-zones moved with a plan; a suggested fit shown, or none to suggest. Words only.

title: When a plan is moved, what was placed on it can move too; A room scan finds its own place; Drawing rooms on a scanned plan, and what to click when lining plans up
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Furnish's Build menu offers "Place the scan's guess"** for the floor showing, so a floor with nothing placed can be filled from its room scan without picking a piece first.

### Added
- **Mapping → Library says when a moved plan has left things behind.** A floor plan's place in the house is corrected now and then: its scale was wrong, its shape squeezed, it was lined up again. Everything put on it (the room traced on it, the receivers pinned on it, the calibration points recorded on it, the lights and sensors in its rooms) is stored in metres, so it stayed where the plan used to be. The plan's row now says so: "This plan was moved: 1 room, 3 receivers and 32 calibration points placed on it still stand where it used to be, up to 1.7 m off."
- **Review lists what could move with it, with nothing ticked.** Tick what should follow the plan and each goes to the same spot on the picture it was on. A backup is taken first, and a move is refused if the backup can't be made. A calibration point's readings, room and label are never touched: only its place.
- **"Leave them where they are"** ends it for that plan without moving anything.
- **A scan uploaded to a floor that already has rooms is placed where it fits.** A scan is in true metres and so are your rooms, so PadSpan lays the scanned room over each drawn room of about its size, at each quarter turn and a little either side, and puts the new plan where the two cover each other best. It says where it went and compares the sizes: "the scan measures 5.7 m by 4.4 m, and Dining Room is drawn 5.9 m by 4.5 m". Where a drawn room is more than a tenth off the scan's measured size, it says the drawn room is off.
- **Only the new plan is placed.** No room, receiver, calibration point or other plan is moved. A scan that fits nowhere, or two rooms equally, is not placed: it starts where every new plan does and says so.
- **A plain rectangle fits both ways round**, so it says to check the doors are on the right walls. Where the 3D house has doors and windows drawn, they settle it.
- **A room's corner lands on the scanned wall end.** On a plan drawn from a room scan, a corner clicked close to a scanned wall end is put exactly on it, so a room traced over a scan matches the scan's own measurements.
- **"Use a scanned outline instead."** Under the drawing buttons on a scanned plan: choose a room, press it, and click inside the scanned room. Its outline becomes that room's, to keep or draw over. Drawing the room yourself stays the first way; this only saves the clicks.
- **Point Align says what to click.** Between plans of two floors it names what runs through both: stairwell corners, an elevator or chimney, a plumbing wall, the house's outside corners.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- The line shown, the list opened, which kinds were moved, left as they are, or a move refused. Words only.
- Whether a scan was placed, placed with its outline fitting both ways, or not placed; and whether the drawn room was over a tenth off the scan's size. Words only.
- A corner landed on a scanned wall end; a scanned outline taken for a room. Words only.

title: Furniture from a phone's room scan; How getting a floor plan goes, in the usage report; Room scans, tuned against real files; Scan upload, checked before release
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **A scanned plan shows the furniture, faintly.** Tables, sofas, beds and the rest are drawn as light outlines where the phone found them, so the plan is recognisable at a glance. Walls stay the darkest thing on it.
- **An L-shaped or stepped room keeps its true outline from a USDZ.** It was read as its bounding rectangle.
- **The scan's wall heights are kept from either file**, USDZ or JSON. Several heights in one room mean a sloped or stepped ceiling.
- **A file that isn't a room scan is refused in plain words**, saying what to share from the scanning app in its place: another tool's own JSON, or a 3D mesh scan with no walls in it.
- **Live Aboard's import takes a RoomPlan USDZ as well as its JSON**, while RoomPlan Import is on in Settings.
- **"Scan the floor with an iPhone or iPad"** in the ways to a plan: a scan gives the floor's walls, and you still say where each room is.

### Fixed
- **A scan file is at most 2.8 MB, and a larger one is refused in plain words.** Home Assistant drops anything bigger on the way in, so the earlier limit could never be reached: a 5 MB file just said "That didn't work". A whole floor's scan is usually under 2 MB.
- **The phone guide's link says why when it can't run.** Opened by someone who isn't an administrator, or on the demo house, it showed plain Mapping and nothing else. It now says what is needed, with a Close button, and waits for the house to load in place of giving up.
- **A damaged or oversized scan file can't tie Home Assistant up.** No more than a scan can hold is ever unpacked, whatever the file claims, and reading it stays quick however the file is made.
- **A scanned plan's furniture guide is dropped when its picture is trimmed, turned or extended**, in place of being drawn in the wrong spots.

### Added
- **"Furniture from scans" in the ⋯ list**, on the 3D house and the flat Map, off unless a screen ticks it. Where a floor plan came from a phone's room scan, the furniture the phone saw is drawn where it stood: faint footprints on the flat Map, pieces in 3D. A guide only, never part of your 3D house, and it moves with its plan.
- **Furnish: "Size to the scan".** Select a piece that stands where the scan found one, and one press gives it the scan's measured width, depth and height. It is not moved or turned.
- **Furnish: "Place the scan's guess".** Under it, one press puts the rest of that room's scanned furniture in as real pieces to drag and change, skipping anything a piece already stands on. One Undo takes them all back.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- Counts of the two Furnish buttons used, and the ⋯ list's new line ticked or unticked, as every other line is.
- **Where each house's plans came from, and how far each kind has got.** A count and a word per kind (a picture, a sketch, a blank floor, a room scan): no scale yet, a scale, rooms drawn, receivers placed, or both. So it can be seen whether a scanned plan goes on to get its rooms, and whether a sketch gets stuck at its scale.
- **The ways to a plan, step by step.** The "No floor plan?" button shown (what every other count is a share of); the phone's walk-through opened from its address, each of its screens reached, closed early or finished; why a scan was refused (too large, wouldn't open, opened but held no room scan, nothing to draw); and of a scan that was read: USDZ or JSON, how many walls as a band, whether the phone had named its rooms, and whether it was given from a phone.
- **Set against the tier in the nightly summary:** how far a house's furthest plan has got, by free, trial and paid.
As ever: words and bands only. Never a file, a name, a size, a picture or a place.

title: The ways to a floor plan, tidied
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **"Ways to get a floor plan" opens straight under its own button**, above the upload form, in place of below the whole page. A room scan and a blank floor each ask which floor they are for, so nothing points at another part of the screen.
- **Handing the scan to someone else's phone is one box.** The guide's address sits in a field with a Copy button, beside "Guide me step by step".
- **Setup's first step and the empty Library say there are other ways** when you have no floor plan: a phone's room scan, your own sketch or a blank floor.
- **Mapping → Layout's floor plan import takes a RoomPlan USDZ as well as its JSON**, while RoomPlan Import is on in Settings: the one reader takes both.

title: No floor plan? Ways to get one, a phone's room scan among them
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Measuring a plan's scale asks for the longest wall you can.** A doorway is too short to trust: a small slip there puts the whole plan out.

### Added
- **Mapping → Upload has "No floor plan? Ways to get one".** Five ways, each with its steps, in the order they are worth trying: a drawing you already have, a room scan from an iPhone or iPad, your robot vacuum's map, your own sketch photographed, and a blank floor. Nothing changes for a picture uploaded the usual way: it is still taken for a proper, to-scale plan.
- **A room scan from an iPhone or iPad Pro becomes a floor plan.** Scan the floor with any app that uses Apple's RoomPlan, share the scan as a USDZ file (or RoomPlan JSON), and pick it in PadSpan. The plan is drawn from the scan's walls, doors and windows, turned so the walls run straight, and to scale: nothing to measure. The ceiling heights and room names in the scan are kept with the plan. Rooms are still drawn on it by hand in this version.
- **A walk-through for the person holding the phone.** "Guide me step by step" shows the scan one step a screen, with big buttons: the right phone, the app, getting the house ready, scanning, saving the file, and giving it to PadSpan. It opens straight from a link, `/padspan-ha?view=maps&guide=scan`, so it can be sent to someone else's phone.
- **A blank floor for a house with no picture at all.** Type the floor's width and depth; PadSpan makes an empty floor of that size with a line every metre, to scale, and opens it for drawing rooms.
- **"This is my own sketch, not to scale"** on the upload. For a sketch, the scale screen takes a length each way and gives each direction its own scale, so both come out right. On any plan, two lengths that disagree now offer "This picture isn't to scale", which does the same. A proper plan's two lengths are averaged as before unless you say so.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- **Which way to a plan people open**, whether a scan or a blank floor was made or refused, and whether a plan was said to be a sketch. Words only: never the file, a size, a name or a picture.
